From: Sara Jones <sara@contoso.com>

Cc: MarketplaceOps <marketplaceops@contoso.com>
Date: 2026-09-12T16:18:00-07:00
Subject: Question on runtime integration for our planned offer

Hi Aditya,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're excited to move forward with listing Contoso Assist on Azure Marketplace and pursuing the co-sell path. Before we begin the publisher registration and manifest submission, the cloud engineering team asked for a short checklist from Redwood covering:

- Runtime endpoints and how multi-tenant routing will be represented in the offer
- Authentication patterns for Azure Marketplace customers vs. direct API keys
- Any required telemetry/audit evidence for co-sell certification (trace level, retention)
- Expected artifact list we must provide during the technical validation gate (manifests, sample ARM templates, container images if any)

I've attached our initial tech requirements spreadsheet with some of their questions. Can you confirm what we should prepare so we can align on a single set of deliverables? We aim to submit the first manifest by the end of next week.

Best,
Sara
Lead Cloud PM, Contoso

Attachment: contoso_tech_requirements.xlsx (xlsx, 78KB)

From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-13T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question on runtime integration for our planned offer

Hi Sara —

Great to hear Contoso is ready to progress. I've sketched a pragmatic set of deliverables below to keep the first validation pass lightweight but sufficient for co-sell enablement:

1) Offer artifacts we expect from you: minimal manifest (SKU mapping + contact info), a sample ARM template showing how a customer would consume the offer (or an integration doc if it's SaaS), and a short network topology diagram.
2) Runtime & auth: our hosted Redwood offering supports Azure AD-backed SSO for customer provisioning (recommended) and token-based API keys for direct integrations. For Azure Marketplace co-sell, customers typically subscribe through the marketplace and we provision a tenant-level API key mapped to their Azure subscription id.
3) Telemetry / evidence: for co-sell technical gate we ask for a list of required observability hooks (trace/span IDs in logs, audit-event retention policy). Redwood can provide sample log schema and a short questionnaire for your infra team.
4) Security proofs: SOC2 type II report + a pointer to any compliance artifacts you have. If you need us to submit Redwood's proofs into your vendor portal, confirm the contact and we'll share links.

I'll loop in Marissa for the marketing/offer packaging checklist and Vivek for publisher account setup steps (we sometimes need tenant-level handshake items for identity binding). Can you confirm the target submission date (you mentioned next Friday)? We'll triage internally and aim to provide a one-page evidence matrix back within 48 hours.

Thanks —
Aditya
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Azure Marketplace next steps & deliverable checklist — Contoso Assist

Hi Sara —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Per our internal review (below are the consolidated deliverables the Contoso engineering team should include for a smooth first validation pass):

Deliverables Contoso should provide before manifest submission:
- Publisher manifest (JSON) with SKU mapping, contact emails, and plan descriptions — sample manifest attached.
- Minimal ARM template or deployment doc that maps the SKU to the subscription-level resource (if SaaS, a short "how a customer onboard" doc is fine).
- Network topology and tenant provisioning steps describing how customers are routed to your tenant (diagram/PDF).
- Security & compliance evidence: pointer to your SOC2/ISO docs or vendor portal; we will reciprocate with Redwood audit links.
- Telemetry sample: one-page log schema and a retention policy (we need to confirm retention window for co-sell evidence).

Suggested offer packaging (to reduce friction):
- Start with a single free trial SKU + paid monthly plan; avoids complex metering for initial publish.
- Provide a short 1-page integration guide that can be surfaced in the Marketplace listing.

Next steps:
1) Contoso provides the artifacts above by EOD Tuesday (2026-09-21) — we'll review and return an evidence matrix within 48 hours.
2) Marissa to review marketing copy / pricing questions and confirm if trial SKU is viable.
3) Vivek to send tenant identity-binding playbook and Redwood SOC2 link (cc'd).

I'll open a shared Drive folder and drop our sample manifest + the evidence checklist. If you prefer a quick sync, I'm available Wednesday morning PST for a 20-minute call.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
